text:
The snapshot looks like mid-2015: unemployment is 5.5%, headline CPI is about 0%, and the fed funds rate is 0.14%. The dollar is up about 14% year on year, which fits the 2014–15 surge. The 10-year yield is 2.33%, up 0.39 over 3 months, and the 2-year is 0.64%.

The 10-year yield was about 1.9% in January/February 2015, rose to about 2.3% in May–June, and was about 2.2% in June. The 20+ year Treasury 3-month return of -9.6% points to a sharp rise in long yields, which fits May or June 2015. Unemployment was 5.5% in both April and May, and 5.3% in June, though the latest published value at the end of May would be 5.5% (May's 5.5% figure was published in early June). Headline CPI YoY was about 0.0% in April and 0.0% in May. Equities were -2.2% over 1m in June 2015 (the S&P fell about 2.1%), and the VIX was about 18.9 at the end of June. Payrolls averaged about 207k over 3 months, which fits the revised figures available at end of June, if unemployment was still 5.3% in June, but it is 5.5% here. This is probably the data available at the end of June, with the May unemployment value of 5.5% as the latest published figure. The June jobs report came out on July 2, so it was not yet published at the end of June. That makes June 2015 the best fit.
